question.text: Two identical particles, each of mass m, are joined by an inextensible string. The string is pulled at its midpoint by a steady force F. The entire arrangement rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. Find the acceleration with which each particle approaches the other.
conditions: force F is applied at the string's midpoint
particles are identical, each of mass m

figure.description: Two particles sit at the ends of a V formed by a single string that runs from one particle to a central point and then to the other particle. At that central point a constant, steady force F pulls horizontally, exactly along the line that bisects the V. Each half of the string makes a 30° angle with this bisecting line, so the two string halves together enclose a 60° angle.

solution.approach: Find the string tension from the force balance where F is applied, then use its component across the centreline to get each particle's acceleration toward the other.

steps.text: At the point where F is applied, the same tension T pulls back along each string segment, each at 30° to the centreline. Since this point carries no mass, these forces plus F must balance.
For one particle, only the string tension T acts on it, directed 30° from the centreline. The component of this tension across the centreline pulls the particle toward the other one.
Divide by the mass to get the acceleration of that particle toward the other one.

common_mistakes.text: Using the full 60° angle between the two string segments in place of the 30° angle each segment makes with the centreline gives (√3/2)(F/m).
Reporting the acceleration along the centreline (toward F) instead of across it toward the other particle gives T cos30°/m = F/(2m).
